WHY_THIS_LOT_EXISTS.necessity_produced_by_a_completed_readin: 🔴 Your own completed reading of PMID 16941225 established that the antibody on which that paper's entire tissue map rests is NOT validated in that paper: no negative control appears anywhere in it, the immunogen is the WW-domain region, and specificity is handed off to these two 2005 papers by citation. Neither has ever been read in this repository. So the corpus's tissue-expression and compartment arguments — which other readings in this batch now lean on — rest on a reagent whose validation sits in two unread papers. The intake had both as Tier-C placeholders of LOW clinical relevance, and by the intake's own criteria that was correct; reading changed the priority, which is exactly the kind of necessity a static priority list cannot see.

SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.the_reagent_question_that_defines_the_lo: For each paper: is the anti-WWOX antibody characterised, and by what evidence? Name the specific controls if they exist — peptide or immunogen block, pre-immune or isotype control, knockdown or overexpression correspondence, correspondence between immunoblot band and immunohistochemical signal, a second independent antibody — and say which are absent. Then state the standard the validation actually reaches. 🔴 An antibody characterised on tumour and normal EPITHELIUM is not thereby validated for CNS staining, where the signal is judged by cell shape without a co-marker: say explicitly what the validation does and does not license.
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.15982416: What does this ovarian series establish — how many cases, which histotypes, which scoring, which statistics, which survival analysis — and what does it NOT establish? Is the outcome association adjusted for stage and grade, or is it univariate?
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.15692750: What does this breast series establish about WWOX loss and estrogen-receptor status — how many cases, which cut-offs, which comparator, which statistics — and what does it NOT establish? Is the ER association a measured correlation or an inference from subgroup proportions?
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.the_hormonal_hypothesis: Both papers sit under the same laboratory's sex-steroid-metabolism hypothesis for WWOX. Report whether either TESTS it or merely frames results by it; a hypothesis restated across papers is not evidence accumulating.

INTERNAL_EDGES.known_from_metadata: Both are Nunez-first with Aldaz last, from the same laboratory and the same period (2005), and both are cited by PMID 16941225 for antibody specificity. Substantial author overlap between them.
INTERNAL_EDGES.what_you_must_verify_rather_than_assume: 🔴 Establish from the artefacts whether the two series share cases, tissue microarrays, blots or scoring runs. If the same antibody lot and the same scoring pipeline produced both, then they are not two independent validations of the reagent, and the corpus should not count them as two. Distinguish independence OF THE DATA from replication PERFORMED BY AN EXTERNAL GROUP; do not infer dependence from an author list alone.

ACQUISITION_HINTS_VERIFIED_2026_09_13.figures_are_the_evidence_again: Both papers are immunohistochemistry and immunoblot series: inspect every available panel at native resolution. A caption is not a panel; captions_only downgrades the receipt. The native surface may be vector art inside the publisher PDF rather than a raster — check before rendering, and measure before calling a value unresolvable. Where a validation control exists, it will be in a figure or a methods paragraph, not in the abstract.

WAVE_3_RESULT.reagent_answer: The delegation reaches IMMUNOBLOT-GRADE validation on epithelial lysates against a cell-line genetic null, and contains NO immunohistochemical control in either paper: 15982416 asserts a fusion-protein pre-absorption 'data not shown', 15692750 has none at all and its only named control times the DAB. Absent in both: no-primary, pre-immune, isotype, peptide block, second antibody, knockdown correspondence in tissue, blot-to-IHC correspondence on the same specimens. 15982416 carries no molecular-weight ladder anywhere in Figure 1 (8x); 15692750 does carry 39 kD/31 kD marks and a loaded blank NEG. lane on each of two gels. It licenses neither CNS immunohistochemistry, nor the 46 kDa identity in the ovarian paper, nor an isoform claim.
WAVE_3_RESULT.chain_finding: 🔴 The specificity citation chain does not terminate in either 2005 paper. Both hand the antibody's characterisation onward to their own ref 12 = PMID 14526170 (Ludes-Meyers 2003), which has no receipt in this ledger. 16941225 -> {15982416, 15692750} -> 14526170.
WAVE_3_RESULT.independence_verdict: ONE reagent validation reported across two tissues, not two independent validations. Shared: antibody at 280 ng/ml, PEO1 null cited to the same 11572989, ACIS platform and its 63/255 floor, the immunostaining protocol (the ovarian paper cites the breast paper for it), the laboratory, 7 of 9 authors, Fox Chase pathology. Not shared: tissue, cases, TMAs, blots, upper scoring boundary. Data largely independent; reagent validation one pipeline. Neither is external replication — the only outside group named in the lot is Guler 2004 (15073846), antibody unstated, queued for that reason.
WAVE_3_RESULT.hormonal_frame: Restated, not tested, and partially disconfirmed within one laboratory's own two tissues: breast ER p=0.0054/0.003 with 'further strengthen the hypothesis'; ovary ER p=0.984, flatly null, only PR at p=0.008 with the authors themselves raising histotype composition and leaving it open. Nothing hormonal measured in either. Field density: 'WWOX AND sex steroid' = 11 records; 'WWOX AND antibody specificity' = 1.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: Quota risk: two sessions were killed by an API limit today, and paper 2 was the pdf_only class whose acquisition might have needed a long cascade.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Pipelined paper 2's acquisition (bytes only, no reading) while paper 1 was still being read, then kept the reading order the contract set.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: Acquisition carries no conclusion and cannot contaminate a blind pass; it only removes the risk that the second paper is unstarted if the session dies.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_differed: Had the session been killed mid-way, paper 2 would have had a fingerprinted surface on disk instead of nothing.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: A peer minted FT-100 for another paper between my read of the queue (highest id FT-099) and my append, its 54 lines unstaged in this shared checkout.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Declared the multi-hop debt with NO FT id — reported UNCHECKED by the cross-check — and carried the entry text verbatim in both dossiers; then minted FT-101 as ONE address for all four antecedents once the peer landed FT-100 at 066b476 and the file went quiet.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: Committing the queue file would have carried a peer's hunk under my message; committing a manifest against a working-tree-only id would have persisted an address resolving in no commit. UNCHECKED is neither passed nor blocked, and the debt stayed durable in my own files throughout.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_differed: Had I forced it, either a peer's work would carry my authorship or every later validation of my manifests would fail on an unresolvable identifier.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: The receipt writer updates the shared state-manifest anchor and appends to the shared hash-chained ledger, both of which a peer was also writing.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Guarded each commit on a diff check — commit only if the ledger adds exactly one line and that line is my own event — and included the anchor lines, which were confined to my own append.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: The guard makes the authorship claim verifiable rather than assumed, and refuses rather than proceeding if the condition fails.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_differed: Without the guard, a concurrent peer append would have been committed under my message.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: Four Europe PMC figure URLs returned 16-byte 'error code: 520' bodies, and the efetch route returned a 9,295-byte refusal stub — all of them sitting in files/ looking like surfaces, and the packet's own procedures then reported a structured surface as present for paper 2 on the strength of that .xml.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Deleted the four 16-byte bodies and renamed the stub efetch_pmc_REFUSAL_STUB_not_a_surface.xml, then screened the real surface (the PDF text layer) directly.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: Neither file is unique material — both are reproducible refusals, and both are recorded in the manifests and dossiers with their measured sizes and routes. Leaving them would have let a later run treat a refusal as a deposit, which is exactly what the packet had already done.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_differed: The suspect-text-layer procedure would have stayed closed on false grounds and the PDF text layer would have gone unscreened.
